title: Choose CYCLEBOOK's visual world
question: The bolder hand is in. Build one, or re-roll.

options.label: The Stack
options.lineage: HyperCard stacks: one-bit cards linked by painted buttons
options.thesis: CYCLEBOOK as a stack of one-bit cards you walk through by button, each card one step of the argument, with Deere yellow and green the only color allowed in.
options.viewport: PULSE as the first card: Q3 FY26 in huge numerals, a dithered revenue exhibit running to the card edge, and painted buttons that walk the argument to the trough and the valuation.
options.risk: Mac nostalgia can read as a gimmick to an executive, and Power BI has no bitmap fonts or dissolves, so the world must live in dither, borders and buttons.

raised.raise: Every assumption control previews its outcome at each step, like a test strip, before you commit.
Every figure block shares one label anatomy: name, period, provenance, value.
Each card commits to one dominant exhibit that runs to the card's edge.

regions.label: painted buttons to the next card

options.label: The Instrument
options.lineage: Creator-hardware desk instruments: keycaps, knobs and a small amber screen
options.thesis: CYCLEBOOK as a desk instrument an analyst plays: scenario keys, a P/E knob, an amber screen that reads out one value at a time, and one Deere-yellow key that runs the case.
options.viewport: PULSE as the instrument's face: the amber screen reading $675.74 against implied value, page keys along the top, Q3 readout modules below, guidance lit in Deere green.
options.case: Beats the leader on both: color-coded function keys are the Bloomberg keyboard's lineage, and keys and knobs map one-to-one onto the model's inputs.
options.risk: Keycap physics in Power BI are shadows and states, not real travel; if the chassis gets too literal it becomes a skeuomorphic toy.

regions.label: amber screen: price vs implied value

options.label: The Cyclorama
options.lineage: Theater cycloramas lit from night through dawn into day
options.thesis: The Deere cycle staged as light: day at the FY2023 peak, night at the FY2026 trough, and today's share price as the first light on the horizon.
options.viewport: A black stage with FY2022–FY2026 earnings drawn as a horizon band, the trough at night, and the latest close as a yellow first-light marker.
options.case: Beats the leader on both: the trough-to-dawn metaphor is the thesis itself (management calls 2026 the bottom of the cycle), and a lit stage reads as premium to an executive.
options.risk: A dark stage with cobalt and rose sits close to the dark-mode neon look models default to; the bands must be hard-edged light, never soft aurora gradients.

regions.label: horizon band: FY22 day to FY26 night
cue list: peak · compression · trough · dawn

options.label: Safelight
options.thesis: The model developed like a print: stepped test strips of implied value at every P/E.
options.viewport: A developer tray of stepped test strips under amber.
options.case: Loses both: amber safelight muddies chart colors and provenance, and no finance reader lives in a darkroom.
options.kept: Test strips: preview every step of an outcome before committing.
options.risk: Amber washes out every color distinction the report depends on.

options.label: Archive Wall
options.lineage: Sneaker archive walls of labeled boxes
options.thesis: Segments and quarters as boxes on a wall, indexed by their end labels.
options.viewport: A wall of end labels with the selected box pulled half out.
options.case: Loses both: a streetwear archive reads as retail, and box walls hide the trends a finance reader compares.
options.kept: One label anatomy on every figure block.
options.risk: Retail energy undercuts a research piece.

options.label: Guide Map
options.lineage: Zoo and garden guide maps of flat color lobes
options.thesis: Deere's segments as land lobes on a guide map.
options.viewport: Three segment lobes sized by sales, one swelling past the frame.
options.case: Loses both: area lobes distort quantities, and a leisure map undercuts high-finance credibility.
options.kept: One dominant exhibit per screen, running to the edge.
options.risk: Playful map energy reads as consumer, not capital markets.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A company-snapshot dashboard at the craft level of FactSet Company Snapshot, Koyfin and Morningstar's stock pages.
canonCard.viewport: A ticker header with price and daily change, KPI tiles, a price chart, and financial and segment tables below.
canonCard.risk: Looks like the tools a hiring manager already uses every day, so it proves craft but not a point of view.
